analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/runtime-outdated-status.md, lines 1-3) and an added bullet in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head lines 986-991). No executable source or config is included in the supplied evidence. The prose describes behavior: the provider acts on `runtime_status{verified:false}` from the coordinator, shows a runtime-integrity line in `darkbloom status`, and triggers one immediate auto-update check at most once per 10 minutes through the existing background updater. The mismatch record expires after 15 minutes. The Swift implementation is not in this batch, so none of that behavior could be verified.

Threat-model relevance: TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket), T-013/T-034 (binary and runtime identity), T-053/T-054 (stale authorization and build acceptance), T-057 (availability), and A-011 (binary hash registry). The status line is a diagnostic only. The docs say it does not grant or remove authorization; routing exclusion remains coordinator-owned.

Questions for the code-bearing pass: (1) Is the `runtime_status` message treated as a trusted instruction only on the authenticated coordinator socket? (2) Does the triggered update reuse the existing SelfUpdater integrity checks (hash/signature verification, quarantine, drain) and avoid bypassing them? (3) Is the rate limit enforced so a repeated coordinator-sent `verified:false` cannot cause update loops? (4) Does the status output avoid exposing sensitive identifiers? None of these can be evaluated from the docs alone, so no finding is made. The docs change introduces no concrete security regression. Because the implementing code was not supplied, I do not set needs_deeper_review for this docs-only batch, but the implementing change should be reviewed on those four points.
